description: Preview, run, deactivate, save, organize or delete a scenario. Preview unfamiliar scenarios before running; inspect applied steps, failures and unrestored effects afterward. Storage changes need suitable undo steps. Saved scenarios are drafts requiring acceptance on the device before running. Reuse existing folders when appropriate. A completed scenario does not guarantee a deterministic app or backend state; overrides and cache edits have different coverage and lifetimes.

deviceId.description: Target device id (auto-selected if one is connected).

folder.description: Folder name for action 'setFolder' — omit to un-file the scenario. Matching an existing folder case-insensitively files it there rather than creating a second one.

id.description: Scenario id (required for preview/run/delete; from get_scenarios).

params.description: Variable values for preview/run, e.g. {storeId:'220'}. Declared defaults fill in the rest.

authoredAgainst.description: App version this was written against.

expectedOutcome.description: What SHOULD happen once applied — this is how a tester tells a bug from expected behavior without asking a developer. Write it.

folder.description: The flow this belongs to — "Checkout", "Login". Reuse a folder from get_scenarios; a scenario nobody can find is a scenario nobody runs.

action.description: Action name on that tool, e.g. upsertOverrideRule, async.setItem, startImpersonation, navigate.

tool.description: Tool id: network | storage | impersonate | route-events | query | time-machine

undoSteps.description: How to reverse effects that have no automatic inverse. Supply these whenever a step writes or removes storage, or deactivation will honestly report the key as unrestored.

vars.description: Declare a variable for every value a tester might want to change (a store id, a user, a status code) instead of freezing it into the steps.

name: scenario_action
